title: Claude must just make one API call. Is that it?
text: Someone assumes Claude sends one API call and Big Query hands back the rows. It doesn't. Every query becomes a job tracked and checked until it's ready. So what does that job actually look like? Ask Claw to pull the top 10 names in a

title: One call, or a tracked job
text: Public data set and sometimes the rows come straight back. That's the synchronous mode. One request that blocks until it's done. But a slower query can't finish inside that window. So it submits instead a job with its own ID checked and paged until it's ready. That job runs inside a billing project.

title: Billing project pays. Location pins it.
text: The project charged for the byte scanned isn't necessarily where the data lives and it's pinned to the location it ran in. Ask for the top 10 names in California from the public names data set. And every later check on that job has to carry the same location back or at 4004s.

title: DONE isn't proof it succeeded
text: Check that job again with the location attached and it comes back clean. But reaching done isn't proof it succeeded. The result can carry an error. So that gets checked before the rows are trusted. and a job still running isn't proof it's stuck. That's what the checking is for. One more thing worth knowing, the field name for more pages isn't the same everywhere list and points use next page token, but a query's own results use page token. Read the wrong one and it comes back empty silently after page one. Every big query

title: Carry-out
text: Job claude runs turns on two habits. Carry the same location on every follow-up call and check for an error before trusting a job marked done. Get those right and both query modes take care of themselves. Your turn. Here's

title: Your turn
text: The prompt. Read it with me. Run a query against the big query public data set. Big query public data USA names USA 1910 current and return the top five names for Texas. Watch three things. Does it pass the same location on every follow-up call? Does it check for an error before trusting a job marked done? And does it use the bundled script instead of a raw request that might miss a page? Lay them in for bear. Clawed Big
